answer: Sybil resistance here is a scarce-plot commit-reveal. A new address may mine only after it posts H(secret, plot_id) for a named knoll in one epoch and, on the next, reveals the secret at a public terrace hearing where three established non-kin peers recompute the hash. Every claimed knoll is written into a shared quill register; if a second applicant reveals the same plot, peers reject it and slash the deposit. The check is mechanical: recompute, compare, refuse duplicates. Mass fake identities then cost a unique plot each, which the register makes visible.
